title: Police won't register my complaint (FIR)
triggers: police said go to another station
thane wale FIR nahi likh rahe

rights.plain_explanation: You can report a cognizable offence at any police station, whatever the area where it happened (a "Zero FIR"). You can also report it by electronic means, then sign within three days.
You must be given a copy of your FIR immediately and free of cost.
If the station refuses, send your complaint in writing by post to the Superintendent of Police. If that fails too, you can apply to the Magistrate.
A Magistrate can order the police to investigate a cognizable case, on an application supported by an affidavit.

do_now: Write your complaint down clearly: what, when, where, who.
Ask the officer to register it as a Zero FIR if they say it's not their area.
Ask for your free copy of the FIR.
If they still refuse, note the officer's name and time, and post your complaint to the SP.
user_at_fault_cases: For some offences punishable with 3 to 7 years, police may first do a short preliminary enquiry (up to 14 days) before registering. That alone isn't a refusal.

escalation.label: Superintendent of Police
escalation.detail: Send the complaint in writing by post to the SP of the district.

escalation.label: Magistrate
escalation.detail: Apply to the Magistrate with an affidavit if the SP doesn't act.

escalation.label: Free legal aid
escalation.detail: Call NALSA on 15100 or visit your District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) at the district court. Women, children, people in custody and people below the income limit get a free lawyer.
